author: Unreal Engine
description:
Over the past few years, working closely with studios and more recently as a Solution Architect at Epic Games, Stéphane Biava has gained first-hand insight into the real challenges teams face when bringing Unreal Engine animation and rigging workflows into production. 

This talk recorded at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026 distills those experiences into a practical narrative, highlighting common pain points, unexpected bottlenecks, and the gap between established workflows and real-time environments. 

Unreal Engine already provides the tools needed to build robust animation pipelines, but the real challenge lies in how those tools are approached. Success comes from rethinking processes to align with Unreal Engine’s paradigm. 

Through concrete examples and real production use cases, this video shares what works, what breaks, and how shifting perspective—rather than replicating familiar workflows—can unlock more efficient and scalable solutions.

title: Real-World Animation & Rigging Challenges in Production | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026

description: Evil Raptor has spent significant effort optimizing their early access game "Far Far West".  Join Tom Looman and Ari Arnbjörnsson as they analyze the profiling data, dissect specific optimizations for the project and explore further opportunities as the game continues development.

author: Unreal Engine
description:
As games increasingly adopt real-time inference, memory footprint and runtime efficiency have become just as critical as raw model quality. 

This talk recorded at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026 explores how Databiomes has worked to optimize AI models for practical, in‑game runtime use—balancing fidelity, performance, energy efficiency, and platform constraints, through close collaboration with AMD. 

Databiomes and AMD walk through key lessons learned from adapting offline‑trained models for real‑time execution in Unreal Engine, including strategies for reducing memory pressure, improving latency, and scaling across a wide range of hardware CPU, GPU, and NPU. 

The session also highlights how AMD technologies and plugins can help developers achieve additional runtime savings, enabling AI features that fit within real‑world performance and memory budgets. Watch to come away with a clearer understanding of what it takes to ship AI in games today.

title: Scaling AI the Smart Way: Memory Footprint and Runtime Efficiency | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026
